Smt. V. Sunita, vs The State Of Telangana, on 13 June, 2023
 Honourable Sri Justice N.V.Shravan Kumar
 Writ Petition No. 13690 of 2023
Order:

entities.text: V. Sunita, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for MA&UD appearing for respondent No.1, Sri.Narasimha Goud, learned standing counsel for HMDA appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3, Sri.Malla Reddy, learned standing counsel for Municipality appearing for respondent No.4.
2.

This writ petition has been filed with the following prayer "declaring that the action of the Respondents more particularly Respondent No.3 in issuing the Letter vide Lr.No.
003112/RDP's/HMDA/Plg/2021 dated 05.05.2023 offering the issuance of Transferable Development Right in lieu of the land for the acquisition of the land to the extent of approx.630 sq.Yards from the Petitioners property despite her refusal as illegal, arbitrary void and contrary to the provisions of Articles 300-A and 21 of the Indian Constitution and HMDA Act 2008 and to direct the Respondent authorities not to take any coercive steps without paying proper compensation to the Petitioner against the acquisition of part of Petitioner's property ."

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of Plot No.38, 39, 43, and 44 in Sy.No.197 at Puppalaguda (V), Gandipet (M), Ranga Reddy District and further submits that respondent No.3 issued Notice vide ::2::
Lr.No.003112/RDP'S/HMDA/Plg/2019/2, dated 05.05.2023 requesting the petitioner to handover the possession of the portion of petitioner's property as gift deed to local body for the purpose of construction Road and upon such act, the petitioner will be entitled for Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) as per Rules 16 and 17 in G.O.Ms.No.168 MA, dated 07.04.2012.
Thereafter, petitioner submitted reply to the notice on 15.05.2023 to respondent Nos.2 and 3 and rejected the offer of TDR grant and refused to give consent to execute the gift deed.

4. while things stood thus, inspite of petitioner's rejection, the respondent No.3 again is requesting the petitioner to give consent along with documents under Section 32, 35 of the HMDA Act, for the public interest.
Aggrieved by the said notice dated 05.05.2023, petitioner has filed writ petition.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner draws attention of this Court to Section 35 of Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority Act, 2008 which reads as under:-
"The Metropolitan Development Authority or the local authority may, with the consent of the owner, acquire land for public purposes by way of according transferable development right through issue of Development Right Certificate in lieu of payment towards cost of land in such manner as may be prescribed:

1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Provided that the transferable development right may be arrived at on the basis of relative land value and equivalent amount of both export and import areas as per the Registration Department records.

Such Transferable Development Right may be utilized as additional built space by the owner who can use this either by himself or transfer it to any other person in full or in part for use in a less developed area as prescribed."

and submits that as per Section 35 of HMDA Act, 2008 is clear that the respondent authority cannot issue TDR without consent of the owner ::3::
and pray this Court to direct the respondent authorities not to interfere in the petitioner's property.
6.

Learned standing counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.2 and 3 on instruction submits that since the petitioner has not given consent for transfer of possession of the property, the respondent authorities would not interfere in the petitioner's property without following due process of law and pray this Court to close the writ petition.

7. Recording the submissions made by the learned counsel on either side and in view of the fact that the respondent authorities would not interfere in the petitioner's property without following due process of law, this Writ Petition is closed.

However, it is made clear that upon any such acquisition proceeding the respondent authorities shall follow due process of law and after putting notice to the petitioner and after giving a fair opportunity of hearing, shall pass appropriate orders in accordance with law and communicate the same to the petitioner.
8. Accordingly, this writ petition is closed.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
